units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Calculate the gradient from the two supplied points and substitute either point into the straight-line equation.
units.summary: Find a line through two points.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Differentiate each polynomial term algebraically and evaluate the derivative at the supplied abscissa.
units.summary: Find a quadratic curve’s gradient at a point.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Subtract the supplied position vectors and reuse the unprinted displacement components in Pythagoras, simplifying the resulting surd.
units.summary: Find a planar displacement vector and its exact magnitude.

exceptions: AS vector topic 9 is mapped to the shared A level runtime topic 10; these are two-dimensional AS vector skills.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Evaluate the supplied cubic at its stated candidate root and conclude from the zero remainder.
units.summary: Verify a polynomial factor using the factor theorem.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Use the factor explicitly printed in (a), divide to obtain the residual quadratic and establish that the residual factor has no real zeros.
units.summary: Prove a cubic has only one real root.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Integrate the polynomial and reciprocal-square terms, substitute a surd upper limit and simplify the exact result.
units.summary: Evaluate a definite power-function integral exactly.

exceptions: Visually verified f(x)=2x+3+12/x² and the integral limits 1 and 2√2. The supplied result is 16+3√2.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Expand the difference quotient for 3x², cancel the common terms and take the increment limit.
units.summary: Prove a quadratic derivative from first principles.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Apply positive-integer binomial coefficients for three terms, then identify the substitution making the original base equal to the proposed decimal.
units.summary: Expand an integer-power binomial and describe its numerical use.

exceptions: Source rendering confirms (2−x/2)^7 and the requested estimate 1.995^7; this is a positive-integer AS binomial expansion.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Find the third angle, use the sine rule to obtain a second side and use the included-angle area formula.
units.summary: Find the area of a triangle from a side and two angles.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Relate the claimed square-metre precision to the limited input accuracy or to the assumption that a real lawn is flat.
units.summary: Explain a precision limitation in a lawn-area model.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Replace sin²(x) by 1−cos²(x), solve the resulting quadratic and place both inverse-cosine solutions in the interval beyond one full turn.
units.summary: Solve a trigonometric equation in an extended degree interval.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Handle the zero-leading-coefficient case separately, then use a negative quadratic discriminant and solve its parameter inequality.
units.summary: Constrain a coefficient when an equation has no real roots.

exceptions: Source and scheme explicitly include the degenerate k=0 case; the discriminant argument applies only after separating that case. The printed target is 0≤k<3/4.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Start from a nonnegative square of square roots, expand it and use positivity to justify the required inequality.
units.summary: Prove a mean inequality for positive inputs.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Choose two negative values, evaluate both sides of the inequality explicitly printed in (a) and show the counterexample.
units.summary: Disprove the mean inequality for negative inputs.

exceptions: Visually verified the left-hand side is √(xy), not xy. Counterexample (b) uses the inequality printed in (a), without needing the proof answer.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Recognise the incorrect index law and the incorrect evaluation of a positive integer power in the supplied attempt.
units.summary: Identify errors in an exponential-equation solution.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Apply the correct index law, divide by the positive exponential factor and use logarithms for the exact input, rejecting a zero exponential value.
units.summary: Solve an exponential equation exactly.

exceptions: Visually verified the original equation is 2^(2x+4)−9(2^x)=0; the +4 belongs inside the exponent. The erroneous attempt remains original printed context.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Find the repeated factor, reuse its unprinted roots and multiplicities in the cubic sketch, then use those roots to identify both possible horizontal translations.
units.summary: Factor a cubic, sketch it and infer possible translations.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Construct the line from its given slope and intercept, recover the unprinted exponential constants, interpret their meanings and reuse them for population and doubling-time predictions.
units.summary: Fit, interpret and use a logarithmic population model.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Give two contextual limitations of long-term constant proportional growth without needing fitted numerical parameters.
units.summary: Critique an exponential population model.

exceptions: Raw (c)(ii) and (d)(ii) each carry a joint (i)–(ii) tariff. Parts (a)–(d) are grouped because the line equation and exponential constants are derived rather than printed.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Differentiate the quadratic, construct its normal at the supplied point and combine the line with a second curve so the linear terms cancel before exponentiating for exact coordinates.
units.summary: Find where one curve’s normal meets a logarithmic curve.

exceptions: Visually verified C₂ is y=x/2+ln(2x); the logarithm is not differentiated in this question.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Combine rectangle and semicircle areas to eliminate depth, derive the perimeter and reuse the unprinted depth expression with positive physical dimensions to explain the radius bound.
units.summary: Construct a pool-perimeter model and its physical domain.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Differentiate the rational-power perimeter expression explicitly printed in (a), solve the stationary equation and substitute the physical radius into the perimeter.
units.summary: Find the minimum of a supplied perimeter model.

exceptions: Visually verified P=2x+250/x+πx/2 and 0<x<√(500/π). The shape uses ordinary semicircle formulae; no additional A level radian-sector skill is required. The mark scheme for (b) reuses the unprinted y expression from (a).

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Compare the two distances from the supplied centre or substitute into the circle equation obtained from the known point.
units.summary: Verify a second point lies on a circle.

units.introduced_year_basis: Official AS sample assessment: assessed skills are within Year 1/AS scope.
units.difficulty_basis: Use radius–tangent perpendicularity to construct one or both tangent lines, then obtain their vertical-axis intercepts and separation; symmetry provides a shorter complete route.
units.summary: Find the separation of two circle-tangent intercepts.
